disease_label_per_paper: Group A streptococcal postpartum endometritis complicated by streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
presentation_summary: Otherwise healthy 42-year-old woman presented about two weeks after an uneventful cesarean section.
She had worsening nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for four days; symptoms began about 10 days after delivery.
She had been taking over-the-counter ibuprofen consistently for postoperative analgesia and had no foul vaginal discharge or bleeding beyond expected lochia.
On emergency department arrival she was tachycardic, tachypneic, and hypotensive with blood pressure 77/52 mmHg.
Exam showed diffusely tender abdomen, mild rebound tenderness, trace blood in the vaginal vault, and no cervical motion tenderness or purulent material on pelvic exam.
Labs showed lactate 4.7 mmol/L, WBC 10.97 k/uL, creatinine 3.28 mg/dL, and bilirubin 2.5 mg/dL.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast showed an enlarged postpartum uterus without localized fluid collection or other major abnormality.
She deteriorated rapidly with refractory shock, PEA arrest, emergent laparotomy, hysterectomy, and death; later blood culture and pathology confirmed GAS suppurative endometritis and TSS.

quality_warnings: GAS blood culture, pathology, autopsy, and final TSS confirmation are preserved as non-ranking evidence.
Absence of fever, foul lochia, cervical motion tenderness, and purulence is retained as rankable negative presentation evidence because invasive GAS postpartum endometritis can be atypical.

The case is expected to rank as postpartum endometritis from postpartum uterine context plus shock and abdominal findings; systemic TSS can be modeled as a superposed or downstream toxin leaf in broader tests.
